n: Hawala and Money or Value Transfer Services for Terrorist Financing
ds: Informal value transfer systems and unregulated or poorly supervised MVTS can move funds across borders using settlement by trade, netting or cash, leaving limited records. They are important to many legitimate communities but can be abused to transfer money to terrorist actors in regions with limited banking access.

src.t: FATF, The Role of Hawala and Other Similar Service Providers in Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing (2013)
FATF, Guidance for a Risk-Based Approach: Money or Value Transfer Services (2016)

cn.rt: Informal value transfer via cash deposits by many people and pooled receipts into everyday accounts; branch cash and remote transfers.

rat: Informal and poorly supervised MVTS operators with pooled accounts, structured cash and trade-based settlement to conflict areas.

ind.n: Operator account with transactions inconsistent with a retail remittance profile
ind.cx: Business accounts of an MVTS or agent receive large pooled deposits and send bulk payments to a small set of foreign counterparties.
ind.ds: Business accounts of an MVTS or agent receive large pooled deposits and send bulk payments to a small set of foreign counterparties.

ind.n: Unlicensed operator or no evidence of registration
ind.cx: Customer offers transfers but cannot evidence registration or supervision.
ind.fp: Small agents of licensed principals may hold no own licence.
ind.ds: Customer offering a regulated or permitted activity cannot evidence the required licence or registration, or operates under a licence held by another party.
ind.cn: Missing, misused or unverifiable licence or registration

ind.n: Structured cash deposits across branches followed by overseas settlement
ind.cx: Numerous cash deposits below thresholds by different people into one account, then wires to settlement partners.
ind.fp: Cash-heavy communities and retail trades show similar patterns.
ind.ds: Cash is deposited in several locations, channels or accounts on the same day or over a short period so that no single deposit stands out.
ind.cn: Cash deposits split across branches, ATMs or accounts

ind.n: Settlement via trade, with mismatched invoices
ind.cx: Offsetting flows are arranged through trade payments unrelated to the underlying goods.
ind.fp: Genuine trade can be netted among related firms.
ind.ds: Offsetting flows are arranged through trade payments unrelated to the underlying goods.

ind.n: Payments to or from higher-risk jurisdictions without clear relationship
ind.cx: Transfers to recipients in conflict-affected areas with no documented relationship or stated purpose.
ind.fp: Many families lack documentation but have genuine needs.
ind.ds: Payments, counterparties or sales originate in or go to countries with no link to the customer, declared business, services or goods.
ind.cn: Payments or activity in jurisdictions unrelated to the customer's business or goods

ind.n: Poor or missing sender and recipient information in transfers
ind.cx: Payment messages lack complete originator or beneficiary details.
ind.fp: Systems limitations may cause incomplete data.
ind.ds: Payment messages omit, truncate or use generic placeholder data for originator or beneficiary details.
ind.cn: Missing, incomplete or placeholder originator and beneficiary information

ind.n: Agent network with rapid expansion in higher-risk locations
ind.cx: Operator adds agents quickly in areas with terrorist presence without strengthened oversight.
ind.fp: Growth in diaspora markets is common.
ind.ds: Operator adds agents quickly in areas with terrorist presence without strengthened oversight.

ind.n: Linked parties with previous suspicious reports or designation
ind.cx: Operator, owners or agents match prior reports, adverse media or designation lists.
ind.ds: Owners, officers or associates match sanctions or designation lists, prior suspicious reports or adverse media.
ind.cn: Ownership or controllers linked to designated or previously reported parties

ctl.ds: Verifies licences, registrations and supervisory status of customers, agents and counterparties against regulator registers before onboarding and periodically. It confirms legal authority to operate and detects unlicensed activity.

Applies targeted enhanced checks to customer types or sectors known to be vulnerable to misuse, such as cash-intensive trades, money service businesses, high-value dealers, professional services, charities or waste handlers. Questions and evidence are tailored to how the sector normally operates.
Detects remitter-like activity, pooled flows and informal channel use on accounts not authorised for money transfer. It finds unregistered MVTS operators and hawala-type settlement.

ctl.n: Account restriction, decline and exit policy
ctl.ds: Defines when a relationship or supplier must be declined, restricted or terminated, for example for unresolved due diligence, non-cooperation or unmanageable risk, with timelines and approvers. It prevents indefinite continuation of relationships that cannot be controlled.
Detects repeated transactions placed just below reporting or approval limits, tuned by band and window per segment. It counters deliberate splitting designed to avoid scrutiny.

Detects, restricts and challenges payments or deposits made by or to parties not named in the contract, account or invoice, and requires evidence of the relationship. It stops accounts and trades being funded by unexplained third parties.

Compares declared unit prices, award values, fees and ancillary costs with reference databases, estimates and comparable contracts, and requires documented rationale for outliers. It detects over- and under-invoicing and inflated awards.

Reconciles trade documents, invoices and shipments with the payments that settle them and reviews settlement made outside standard banking channels. It exposes trade-based laundering where payment logic does not match the underlying deal.

ctl.n: Fan-in, fan-out and funnel account detection
ctl.ds: Detects accounts receiving from many unrelated senders, or sending to many beneficiaries, followed by consolidation or onward movement. It surfaces collector, funnel and mule structures.

Applies enhanced review, approval, limits and conditions to relationships or flows that involve jurisdictions rated higher risk for secrecy, corruption, conflict or weak controls. Triggers include nationality, residence, counterparties and payment routing.

ctl.n: Payment message completeness and quality controls
ctl.ds: Rejects or queries payments with missing or meaningless party data, tracks deficiency rates and resubmissions and scorecards senders. It improves transparency of payment chains.

Sends requests for information to respondents or senders with deadlines, tracking of response quality and escalation of repeated deficiencies. It resolves unexplained activity and pressures partners to improve.

ctl.n: Agent and distribution network due diligence
ctl.ds: Vets, trains, caps and monitors agents, sub-agents and distributors who onboard customers or move funds on the institution's behalf, including quality visits, outlier analysis and disclosure of principals. It limits control failures at the edge of a distribution network.
Checks parties against previously filed internal reports, links to reported accounts and feeds report outcomes back into tuning. It spots repeat subjects and sharpens detection.

Screens customers, owners, counterparties, vessels, dealers and addresses against sanctions, enforcement and restricted-party lists at onboarding and ongoing, using fuzzy matching and secondary identifiers. Potential matches are held for adjudication before service or funds are released.
